title: EFS and FSx: shared file systems

kcs.statement: Amazon EFS is a managed NFS file system for Linux that many EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones can mount at once. It grows and shrinks automatically and is billed per GB stored.
EFS lifecycle management moves files that have not been accessed for a chosen period to the lower-cost EFS Infrequent Access storage class.

Amazon FSx provides fully managed third-party file systems: FSx for Windows File Server (SMB, Active Directory integration), FSx for Lustre (high-performance computing and ML), and FSx for NetApp ONTAP and OpenZFS.

problem_ideas: A Linux web fleet across three AZs must share uploaded files: which service?
A Windows app needs SMB shares joined to Active Directory: which service?
An ML team needs a file system with very high throughput fed from S3 for training: which FSx flavour?
Files untouched for 60 days make up 80% of an EFS file system: name the feature that cuts cost.
A distractor offers EBS for 50 instances sharing one folder: why does it fail?
Match four requirements to EFS, FSx for Windows, FSx for Lustre or FSx for NetApp ONTAP.
